A1.justification: Both PDFs describe BADiff and contain readable main text, figures, tables, equations, references, and Appendices A–H. Inspection supports reliable comparison throughout both 19-page documents.

before.justification: v2 reports original generation-quality, bitrate-error, latency, ablation, high-resolution, text-to-image, and teacher-label cost results in Sections 4.2–4.7 and Tables 1–6.

after.justification: v3 retains the work's original empirical results in Sections 4.2–4.7 and Tables 1–6, including benchmark comparisons, component ablations, and computational measurements.

M1.justification: Sections 3.2–3.5 and Algorithms 1–2 retain the same entropy conditioning, four training losses, and adaptive stopping procedure. New Figure 2 illustrates existing components; renaming the pooled feature from h_t to z_t does not change the method.

E1.justification: Both retain CIFAR-10, CelebA-HQ, and LSUN benchmarks, 512- and 1024-resolution experiments, Stable Diffusion text-to-image evaluation, and COCO-val2017 teacher-cost measurements. The experiments described as new in Section 4.5 already appear in v2.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged within Tables 1, 2, 4, and 5. The same BPG/LIC cascades, Early-Stop, PNDM, and DPM-Solver participate in their respective comparisons; v3 only reformats the baseline list.

E3.justification: Backbones, bitrate intervals, preprocessing statements, metrics, and training budgets remain unchanged. Latency still averages 1,000 test samples after 50 warm-up iterations. Settings removed from the main-text training paragraph remain in Appendix E and Table 7.

E4.justification: Section 4.4 and Table 3 retain the same conditioning, hinge-loss, and calibration-loss ablations. The supplementary predictor-approximation and complexity analyses also remain unchanged. The new training diagram supplies no additional experimental analysis.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-training-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests. The existing latency-averaging procedure is unchanged, and v3 adds no uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: Tables 1–6 retain all numerical entries and rankings. For example, low-bitrate CIFAR-10 BADiff with DDPM still reports FID 11.4 and latency 65 ms. High-resolution, text-to-image, ablation, and teacher-cost findings are also unchanged.

T1.justification: Section 3.1 condenses standard diffusion background, with the forward and reverse transition formulations retained in Appendix A. The entropy derivation, gradient analysis, predictor-error bound, and complexity reasoning remain unchanged; equation renumbering and feature notation changes are nonsubstantive.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction contributions, and conclusion retain the same novelty, bandwidth compliance, perceptual-quality, and computational-efficiency claims. Shortening Figure 1's caption does not remove the computation-saving claim maintained elsewhere.

C2.justification: v3 removes Section 4.1's explicit assertion that BADiff remains bandwidth-adaptive when combined with any fast ODE solver. Section 5 still identifies PNDM/DPM-Solver integration as future work. This trims an applicability argument; other interpretations and limitations remain unchanged.

D1.justification: The deleted main-text training paragraph duplicates optimizer, iteration-count, and loss-weight information retained in Appendix E and Table 7. Architecture specifications, hardware/software details, codec implementations, and the code-access statement are unchanged.

R1.justification: The 58 references and Section 2 are unchanged. However, deleting the Section 4.1 orthogonality remark removes an explicit explanation of BADiff's complementarity with PNDM and DPM-Solver, slightly reducing its positioning relative to existing acceleration methods.

P1.justification: v3 condenses Section 3.1, moves the algorithm explanation from page 6 to page 7, removes the duplicate training summary, reformats the baseline list, and makes spelling and cross-reference edits. These are localized revisions within an otherwise stable document structure.

P2.justification: Figure 1 is substantially redesigned into two separated, left-to-right transmission pipelines. New Figure 2 provides a full training overview connecting existing modules and four losses. Together these substantially expand and revise the visual explanation, while Tables 1–7 retain their content and structure.

improvement.justification: The clearer Figure 1, new training overview in Figure 2, and condensed background make BADiff easier to follow while preserving its empirical evidence and technical documentation. Removing the explicit solver-compatibility explanation loses some context, but the visual and editorial benefits support a limited overall improvement. No new experimental validation or substantive theoretical correction is added.
